what_it_does: Training large AI models requires feeding enormous datasets into GPUs as fast as possible; when that data is stored in object storage (a cloud storage system like Amazon S3 that stores files as self-contained 'objects'), it must travel from the storage system through the server's main CPU and then to the GPU, which wastes CPU time and creates a bottleneck. OS2G (Object Storage to GPU) moves the data transfer work onto a DPU — a Data Processing Unit, a specialized networking chip found in modern servers that can handle data movement tasks independently of the main CPU. The DPU receives data from the storage system, decompresses and reformats it into the shape the GPU expects, and then sends it directly into GPU memory using a direct chip-to-chip data transfer mechanism (called RDMA — Remote Direct Memory Access — which lets one device write into another's memory without involving the CPU). The main CPU is freed for other work, GPU training utilization improves, and the data pipeline no longer bottlenecks on the host processor.
